```{r read in data}

#ASV Table generated via qiime2 with moving picture tutorial. Supplemental code is also available on the GitHub.

#Read in full ASV table with all taxonomies.
asv_input = read.table(file="./_final_ASV_table_noContam.tsv", header=T, sep = "\t")

num_otu_single_sample = asv_input %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  summarize(single_sample = sum(c_across(-c(1, 2:13)) > 0) == 1) %>%
  summarize(sum(single_sample)) %>%
  pull()

#Split up just taxonomy to keep it separated.
asv_taxonomy = asv_input %>%
  select(c(otu_id, gtdb, gtdb_conf, silva, silva_conf))

#Now lets make just an ASV table with all samples.
asv_table_df = asv_input %>%
  select(-c(gtdb, gtdb_conf, silva, silva_conf)) %>%
  column_to_rownames(var="otu_id")
 
#Let's now subset that to only those that from the control samples we wanted to compare.
asv_table_controls_df = asv_table_df %>%
  select(-c(8:87)) %>%
  select(-c("Lys")) #This was an extra sample that got thrown in the sequencer

#And let's make another one that is just the samples that we want to study re: experimental design questions.
asv_table_experiment_df = asv_table_df %>%
  select(-c(1:7)) %>%
  select(-c("S33", "S65", "S66", "S67")) #remove these 4 which were QC samples.

#write.csv(asv_table_experiment_df, file="_final_ASV_filtered_SITES.csv")

#I rolled these up at the GTDB genera level so i'm going to read those in now.
genera_rollup_input = read.table(file="./_final_genera_taxonomic_overlap_noContam.txt", header=T, sep = "\t", row.names=1)
  
genera_rollup_experiment_df = genera_rollup_input %>%
  select(-c("S33", "S65", "S66", "S67")) #remove these 4 which were QC samples.  

#write.csv(genera_rollup_experiment_df, file="_final_genera_filtered_SITES.csv")

metadata_table = read.table(file="./_sample_metadata_final_87samples.tsv", header=T, row.names = 1, sep = "\t")

metadata_table_control_df = metadata_table %>%
  dplyr::slice(2:7)

metadata_table_experiment_df = metadata_table %>%
  dplyr::slice(-c(1:7)) %>%
  filter(!grepl("QC", sample_type))

chemistry_df = read.table(file="./ccp_chemistry_76sample_final.txt", header=T, sep = "\t")

#There are a handful of measurements here that I need to remove because there are not enough of them. Going to remove any measurement that is not present across at least 30 samples.
chemistry_df_final = chemistry_df %>%
  select(-c(Ag, Br, P, U))

#Making a metadata table from the chemistry df itself:
chemistry_metadat = chemistry_df_final %>%
  select(c(1:4))

# Select and rename the 'site' column to 'Site' while ensuring it's of type character
metadata_selected = metadata_table_experiment_df %>%
  select(Site = site, region) %>%
  distinct(Site, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(Site = as.character(Site))

# Ensure 'Site' in chemistry_metadat is of type character
chemistry_metadat = chemistry_metadat %>%
  mutate(Site = as.character(Site))

# Merge the region column into the chemistry_metadat dataframe by the Site column
chemistry_metadat = chemistry_metadat %>%
  left_join(metadata_selected, by = "Site")

#Now lets organize the chem table
chemistry_df_withNA_input = chemistry_df_final %>%
  column_to_rownames(var="site_id") %>%
  select(-c(1:3)) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric)) #make numeric because it'll yell if not below.

#Ho boy. Lot of chemistry that is missing values here. Going to have to chop some of these off. Also - there are a significant amount of negative numbers in this dataset. There is no such thing as negative measurement here, except for ORP. Lets make everything that is less than 0 just a 0.

chemistry_df_final_input_chemChop = chemistry_df_withNA_input %>%
  select(-c(alk_bicarb, alk_carb, alk_total, Cl, Cu, DO, Mn, Ni, Mg, ORP, ph_lab, TURB, Zn)) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ ifelse(. < 0, 0, .)))

variables_to_keep = c("asv_taxonomy", "asv_table_controls_df", "asv_table_experiment_df", "metadata_table_control_df", "metadata_table_experiment_df", "chemistry_df_final", "genera_rollup_experiment_df", "genera_rollup_experiment_df_rel", "chemistry_df_final_input_chemChop")

rm(list=setdiff(ls(), variables_to_keep)) #clean out the environment.

```

```{r Bulk community-level statistics}

#First, let's start off with some PERMANOVA's and some NMDS to see if communities are unique across these different conditions.

#Let's make these relative abund
asv_table_controls_df_rel = asv_table_controls_df %>%
    mutate(across(everything(), ~ . / sum(.))) %>%
  filter(rowSums(.)!=0)

# PERMANOVA for controls
dm.asv_control=calc_dm(asv_table_controls_df_rel, method = "bray")
adonis2(formula = dm.asv_control ~ sample_type, data = metadata_table_control_df, permutations = 999)

#Looks like none of the controls are significantly different, which is good and what we hoped. Data is spotty though. So let me try subsetting to a shared subset across controls.

group1 = c("R01", "R02")
group2 = c("R4C1", "R4C2")
group3 = c("RRT1", "RRT2")

# Define the groups as lists
groups = list(group1, group2, group3)

# Create a function to check presence in groups
check_presence_in_groups = function(df, groups) {
  apply(df, 1, function(row) {
    sum(sapply(groups, function(group) {
      any(row[group] != 0)
    }))
  })
}

# Filter the rows for presence in at least 2 groups
asv_table_controls_df_rel_2groups = asv_table_controls_df_rel %>%
  filter(check_presence_in_groups(select(., group1, group2, group3), groups) >= 2)

#Now lets check the shared subset:

dm.asv_control_min2=calc_dm(asv_table_controls_df_rel_2groups, method = "bray")
adonis2(formula = dm.asv_control_min2 ~ sample_type, data = metadata_table_control_df, permutations = 999)

####################




#Let's make the experimental samples relative abund
asv_table_experiment_df_rel = asv_table_experiment_df %>%
      mutate(across(everything(), ~ . / sum(.)))

# PERMANOVA for experiment
dm.asv_experiment=calc_dm(asv_table_experiment_df_rel, method = "bray")
adonis2(dm.asv_experiment ~ site, data = metadata_table_experiment_df, permutations = 999)
adonis2(dm.asv_experiment ~ sample_type, data = metadata_table_experiment_df, permutations = 999)

#Need to remove the PW samples from this comparison as they are not influenced by region.
PW_samples = c("S108", "S15", "S17", "S18", "S19", "S20", "S21", "S22",
                "S23", "S24", "S26", "S31", "S32", "S34", "S36", "S38",
                "S39", "S40", "S41", "S42", "S43", "S45", "S47", "S49",
                "S51", "S53", "S55", "S60", "S64", "S68", "S76", "S77",
                "S82", "S83", "S84", "S93", "S95", "S98")

PW_samples_nums = sub("^S", "", PW_samples)

#Remove specified columns from rel abund
asv_table_experiment_df_rel_noPW = asv_table_experiment_df_rel[ , !(names(asv_table_experiment_df_rel) %in% PW_samples)]

#Remove the rows from metadat
metadata_table_experiment_df_noPW = metadata_table_experiment_df[!(metadata_table_experiment_df$sample_num %in% PW_samples_nums), ]

dm.asv_experiment_noPW=calc_dm(asv_table_experiment_df_rel_noPW, method = "bray")
adonis2(dm.asv_experiment_noPW ~ region, data = metadata_table_experiment_df_noPW, permutations = 999)

#Interesting, these communities do not appear to be significantly different to each other by "Upgradient, Downgradient, or Porewater" or site or region. Which makes sense as these are fairly different locations. 

#Let's make the genera level rollup relative
genera_rollup_experiment_df_rel = genera_rollup_experiment_df %>%
        mutate(across(everything(), ~ . / sum(.)))

# PERMANOVA for experiment genera rollup
dm.genera_experiment=calc_dm(genera_rollup_experiment_df_rel, method = "bray")
adonis2(dm.genera_experiment ~ site, data = metadata_table_experiment_df, permutations = 999)
adonis2(dm.genera_experiment ~ sample_type, data = metadata_table_experiment_df, permutations = 999)

#Remove specified columns from rel abund
genera_rollup_experiment_df_rel_noPW = genera_rollup_experiment_df_rel[ , !(names(genera_rollup_experiment_df_rel) %in% PW_samples)]

dm.genera_experiment_noPW=calc_dm(genera_rollup_experiment_df_rel_noPW, method = "bray")
adonis2(dm.genera_experiment_noPW ~ region, data = metadata_table_experiment_df_noPW, permutations = 999)

#These genera-level rollups are not significantly different. Only by site.

#Let's do some NMDS on these ordinations.

#

## It looks like generas at a community level are not significantly different. However, I bet there are a handful of generas that would fall out of an indicator analysis for some of the treatments. lets see if any generas are indicators of treatments, and whether those genera taxonomies are unique.
#
#

genera_table_experiment_df_min1 = genera_rollup_experiment_df_rel %>%
  filter(rowSums(. > 0) >= 1)

genera_table_experiment_df_min2 = genera_rollup_experiment_df_rel %>%
  filter(rowSums(. > 0) >= 2)

set.seed(1234)
indic.genera = multipatt(t(genera_table_experiment_df_min2), metadata_table_experiment_df$sample_type, duleg = F, func = "r.g", permutations = 9999)

indic.genera = indic.genera$sign
indic.genera$genera_id = rownames(indic.genera)
indic.genera$p.fdr = p.adjust(indic.genera$p.value, method = "fdr")

# Nada



#Alright, so it looks like these communities are just not that different at a microbial level at a sample type - level, which is interesting and would suggest that treatments are working. However, ASVs are different at the site level which is interesting, i'll address those in the section below. For now, let's just make a heatmap here that will showcase this the easiest at a genera-level.

genera_rollup_experiment_heatmap_df = genera_rollup_experiment_df %>%
  rownames_to_column(var="genera_id")

#There's a whole bunch of genera here that are super low abundance. So lets just make this cleaner by plotting only those genera that have more than 0.5% of total abundance. Random cutoff.

# Step 1: Calculate the total abundance for each genus
genera_totals = rowSums(genera_rollup_experiment_heatmap_df[, -1])

# Step 2: Calculate the threshold for 0.5% of the overall population
total_abundance = sum(genera_totals)
threshold = total_abundance * 0.005

# Step 3: Separate the genera that are above the threshold and those that are below it
above_threshold = genera_rollup_experiment_heatmap_df[genera_totals >= threshold, ]
below_threshold = genera_rollup_experiment_heatmap_df[genera_totals < threshold, ]

# Step 4: Sum the abundance of the below-threshold genera by column
below_threshold_sum = colSums(below_threshold[, -1])

# Step 5: Create a new row for the aggregated below-threshold genera
new_row = data.frame(genera_id = "under 0.5% of abundance", t(below_threshold_sum))
colnames(new_row) = colnames(genera_rollup_experiment_heatmap_df)

# Ensure both data frames have the same column names and types
above_threshold = as.data.frame(above_threshold)
new_row = as.data.frame(new_row)

# Step 6: Combine the above-threshold genera with the new row
```

```{r Site-level statistics - OTUs & Genera}
#Super loosey-goosey here. Let's just run an nmds. I know the stress is off. And i know i need to further filter.

# Function to perform metaMDS per site
run_metaMDS = function(df, metadata, site_column) {
  sites = unique(metadata[[site_column]])
  nmds_list = list()
  
  for (site in sites) {
    # Filter metadata for the current site
    site_metadata = metadata[metadata[[site_column]] == site, ]
    
    # Extract sample names for the current site
    sample_names = rownames(site_metadata)
    
    # Filter ASV table based on these sample names
    site_asv = df[, sample_names, drop = FALSE]
    
    # Debugging: print out the samples being pulled
    cat("Processing site:", site, "\n")
    cat("Samples in metadata for site", site, ":\n")
    print(sample_names)
    cat("Samples in ASV table for site", site, ":\n")
    print(colnames(site_asv))
    
    # Assign filtered DataFrames to global environment
    assign(paste0("metaMDS_", site, "_asv_df"), site_asv, envir = .GlobalEnv)
    assign(paste0("metaMDS_", site, "_metadata_df"), site_metadata, envir = .GlobalEnv)
    
    # Ensure there are columns/rows to process
    if (ncol(site_asv) > 1 && nrow(site_metadata) > 1) {
      # Calculate NMDS
      nmds_result = metaMDS(t(site_asv), distance = "bray", noshare = TRUE, trace = 1, autotransform = TRUE, trymax = 999)
      
      # Extract scores and add metadata
      scores_df = as.data.frame(scores(nmds_result)$sites)
      scores_df$sample_type = site_metadata$sample_type
      scores_df$SampleID = rownames(scores_df)
      scores_df$sample_point = site_metadata$sample_point
      scores_df$site = site
      scores_df$region = site_metadata$region

      # Append to list
      nmds_list[[site]] = scores_df
    }
  }
  
  # Combine all NMDS results into one data frame
  combined_nmds_df = do.call(rbind, nmds_list)
  
  return(combined_nmds_df)
}

# Split data and run metaMDS for each site
combined_nmds_df = run_metaMDS(asv_table_experiment_df_SITES_rel, metadata_table_experiment_df_SITES, "site")

# Define custom colors and shapes

shape_values = c("Ash Pond Water" = 15,

                  "GW-Downgradient" = 17,
                  "GW-Upgradient" = 18)

combined_nmds_df = combined_nmds_df %>%

  ))

# Function to perform adonis2 per site
run_adonis2_per_site = function(df, metadata, site_column, sample_type_column) {
  sites = unique(metadata[[site_column]])
  adonis2_results = list()
  
  for (site in sites) {
    # Filter metadata for the current site
    site_metadata = metadata[metadata[[site_column]] == site, ]
    
    # Extract sample names for the current site
    sample_names = rownames(site_metadata)
    
    # Filter ASV table based on these sample names
    site_asv = df[, sample_names, drop = FALSE]
    
    # Debugging: print out the samples being pulled
    cat("Processing site:", site, "\n")
    cat("Samples in metadata for site", site, ":\n")
    print(sample_names)
    cat("Samples in ASV table for site", site, ":\n")
    print(colnames(site_asv))
    
    # Ensure there are columns/rows to process
    if (ncol(site_asv) > 1 && nrow(site_metadata) > 1) {
      # Calculate Bray-Curtis distance matrix
      dm = vegdist(t(site_asv), method = "bray")
      
      # Run adonis2
      adonis2_result = adonis2(formula = dm ~ sample_type, data = site_metadata, permutations = 999)
      
      # Store result
      adonis2_results[[site]] = adonis2_result
    }
    
    # Assign filtered DataFrames to global environment
    assign(paste0("function_ADONIS_", site, "_asv_df"), site_asv, envir = .GlobalEnv)
    assign(paste0("function_ADONIS_", site, "_metadata_df"), site_metadata, envir = .GlobalEnv)
  }
  
  return(adonis2_results)
}


# Run adonis2 for each site, testing the effect of sample_type

  sqrt((x-home[1])^2 + (y-home[2])^2)
}

         plot_pc2 = ifelse(top_c == "top", NMDS2, 0),
         top_label = ifelse(top_c == "top", Compound, "")) %>%

#Let me try to plot this a little more creatively while running some stats:
chem_features = rownames(t(chemistry_df_final_input_chemChop_SITES_FINAL_46001))
nmds_scores = as.data.frame(scores(NMDS_Bray_SiteNMDS_46001)$sites)

# Initialize correlation results dataframe
cor_results = data.frame(Feature = chem_features,
                         R_NMDS1 = numeric(length(chem_features)),
                         p_value_NMDS1 = numeric(length(chem_features)),
                         R_NMDS2 = numeric(length(chem_features)),
                         p_value_NMDS2 = numeric(length(chem_features)))

# Calculate Spearman correlations
for (i in 1:length(chem_features)) {
  feat = chem_features[i]
  cor_test_NMDS1 = cor.test(nmds_scores$NMDS1, chemistry_df_final_input_chemChop_SITES_FINAL_46001[, feat], method = "spearman")
  cor_test_NMDS2 = cor.test(nmds_scores$NMDS2, chemistry_df_final_input_chemChop_SITES_FINAL_46001[, feat], method = "spearman")
  
  cor_results$R_NMDS1[i] = cor_test_NMDS1$estimate
  cor_results$p_value_NMDS1[i] = cor_test_NMDS1$p.value
  cor_results$R_NMDS2[i] = cor_test_NMDS2$estimate
  cor_results$p_value_NMDS2[i] = cor_test_NMDS2$p.value
}

# Pivot longer for plotting
corrs_pivot_longer = cor_results %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("R_"), names_pattern = "R_(.*)", names_to = c("NMDS_Axis"), values_to = "R") %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("p_value_"), names_pattern = "p_value_(.*)", names_to = c("NMDS_Axis_pval"), values_to = "p_value") %>%
  filter(NMDS_Axis == NMDS_Axis_pval) %>%
  select(-NMDS_Axis_pval)

# Create the scatter bubble plot
scatter_bubble = ggplot(corrs_pivot_longer, aes(x = Feature, y = R, size = (1-p_value), color = NMDS_Axis, shape = NMDS_Axis)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "Chemistry Feature", y = "Spearman Correlation (R)", size = "p-value", 
       shape = "NMDS Axis", color = "NMDS Axis") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey") +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-1, 1, by = 0.5), limits = c(-1, 1)) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.3)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("NMDS1" = "#ffa439", "NMDS2" = "#c5e67b"))

scatter_bubble
```

```{r Bulk community-level statistics - Chemistry}
#Now let's do some PERMANOVA's and some NMDS to see if chemistry are unique across these different conditions.

#Making a metadata table from the chemistry df itself:
chemistry_metadat = chemistry_df_final %>%
  select(c(1:4))

# Select and rename the 'site' column to 'Site' while ensuring it's of type character
metadata_selected = metadata_table_experiment_df %>%
  select(Site = site, region) %>%
  distinct(Site, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(Site = as.character(Site))

# Ensure 'Site' in chemistry_metadat is of type character
chemistry_metadat = chemistry_metadat %>%
  mutate(Site = as.character(Site))

# Merge the region column into the chemistry_metadat dataframe by the Site column
chemistry_metadat = chemistry_metadat %>%
  left_join(metadata_selected, by = "Site")

#Now lets organize the chem table
chemistry_df_withNA_input = chemistry_df_final %>%
  column_to_rownames(var="site_id") %>%
  select(-c(1:3)) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric)) #make numeric because it'll yell if not below.

#Ho boy. Lot of chemistry that is missing values here. Going to have to chop some of these off. Also - there are a significant amount of negative numbers in this dataset. There is no such thing as negative measurement here. Lets make everything that is less than 0 just a 0.

chemistry_df_final_input_chemChop = chemistry_df_withNA_input %>%
  select(-c(alk_bicarb, alk_carb, alk_total, Cl, Cu, DO, Mn, Ni, Mg, ORP, ph_lab, TURB, Zn)) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ ifelse(. < 0, 0, .)))

# PERMANOVA for controls
dm.chem_control=calc_dm(t(chemistry_df_final_input_chemChop), method = "bray")
adonis2(formula = dm.chem_control ~ Sample.Type, data = chemistry_metadat, permutations = 999)
adonis2(formula = dm.chem_control ~ Site, data = chemistry_metadat, permutations = 999)

#Remove specified columns from rel abund
chemistry_df_final_input_chemChop_noPW = chemistry_df_final_input_chemChop[!rownames(chemistry_df_final_input_chemChop) %in% PW_samples, ]

#Remove the rows from metadat
chemistry_metadat_noPW = chemistry_metadat %>%
  filter(!(site_id %in% PW_samples))

dm.asv_experiment_chem_noPW=calc_dm(t(chemistry_df_final_input_chemChop_noPW), method = "bray")
adonis2(dm.asv_experiment_chem_noPW ~ region, data = chemistry_metadat_noPW, permutations = 999)

#I'm not going to go super deep into the region stuff, so im just going to remove this.
chemistry_metadat = chemistry_metadat %>%
  select(-c(region))

#Looks like Sample Type and Site are both significantly different here. Let's do some pairwise comparisons.

chemical_data_formerge = as.data.frame(chemistry_df_final_input_chemChop)

# Ensure metadata rows match the sample IDs in chemical_data
metadata = chemistry_metadat[chemistry_metadat$site_id %in% rownames(chemical_data_formerge), ]

# Add Sample IDs as a column
chemical_data_formerge$site_id = rownames(chemical_data_formerge)

# Merge chemical data with metadata
chem_merged = chemical_data_formerge %>%
  inner_join(metadata, by = 'site_id') %>%
  select(-c(Sample.Point))

# Automatically identify chemical columns (excluding metadata columns)
metadata_columns = c('site_id', 'Sample.Type', 'Site') # Add any other columns that are not chemical measurements
chemical_columns = setdiff(colnames(chem_merged), metadata_columns)

# Run Kruskal-Wallis for each chemical value and perform pairwise Wilcoxon post-hoc
kw_results = list()
wilcox_results = list()
significant_kws = list()
significant_wilcox = list()

for (chemical_col in chemical_columns) {
  # Kruskal-Wallis test (
  kw_result = kruskal.test(as.formula(paste(chemical_col, "~ Sample.Type")), data = chem_merged)
  kw_p_value = kw_result$p.value
  kw_results[[chemical_col]] = kw_result
  
  # Check if Kruskal-Wallis is significant (p-value < 0.05)
  if (kw_p_value < 0.05) {
    significant_kws[[chemical_col]] = kw_result
    
    # Post-hoc pairwise Wilcoxon test with Bonferroni correction
    wilcox_result = pairwise.wilcox.test(chem_merged[[chemical_col]], chem_merged$Sample.Type, 
                                          p.adjust.method = "bonferroni")
    
    # Filter significant results (account for NA in p-value matrix)
    if (any(wilcox_result$p.value < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)) {
      significant_wilcox[[chemical_col]] = wilcox_result
    }
  }
}

# Print significant pairwise Wilcoxon results
cat("\nSignificant Pairwise Wilcoxon Test results:\n")
print(significant_wilcox)

           aes(fill = Compound))  +
  scale_fill_manual(values=wes_palette("FantasticFox1", type="continuous", 26)) + 
  geom_text(aes(label = Compound, angle=90)) +
  labs(y = "Scaled PC1 Loadings of Significant Compounds",
       x = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "none")
```
